title: Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens endorses Republican Mike Rogers for Senate in Michigan
dek: Two days before the election, the congresswoman who lost the Democratic primary backs her party's opponent. Democratic leaders call it a betrayal, and Republican accounts call it a verdict on the nominee.
what: CNBC reports that Representative Haley Stevens, a Michigan Democrat, said in a video posted to X on Sunday 1 November that she is endorsing Republican Mike Rogers for the US Senate over Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed. CNBC says El-Sayed narrowly beat her in the August primary. It quotes her saying she does not stand with the streamer Hasan Piker, and that El-Sayed had told her to stay away from his campaign: "I don't belong in Abdul's campaign." I have not found El-Sayed's account of that exchange.

El-Sayed, standing with Democratic allies, said "I actually don't think about Haley Stevens" and turned to costs families face, CNBC reports. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer called the endorsement "a despicable betrayal." The Michigan Democratic Party chair, Curtis Hertel, said she "is not a current member of the Michigan Democratic Party, nor will she be in the future." CNBC says President Trump called her "a Highly Respected Democrat" on Truth Social.

Video posted that day shows Stevens saying that when someone says you are not welcome in a campaign, you take the message. Another video shows Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson answering questions about her: Trump says he plans to reach out to thank her, and Johnson says he sent her a note.
why: It is a defection inside a Senate race, it lands two days before voting, and each side can read it as proof of its own view of the nominee.

worlds.name: Republican-leaning accounts
worlds.sees: A sign that Democrats cannot stomach their own nominee. Her words about Hasan Piker are quoted as a reason for Michigan voters to follow her.

worlds.name: Democratic leaders and allies
worlds.sees: A betrayal. They say what is on the ballot is working people's healthcare, rent and bills, and that she has backed the Republican over her own party's nominee.

common: Established by CNBC: Stevens endorsed Rogers on 1 November and gave Hasan Piker and being told she was unwelcome in El-Sayed's campaign as her reasons; Schumer and the state party chair responded as quoted. Not established: that El-Sayed or his campaign told her to stay away, since only her account of it is reported here. Whether the endorsement moves any voters is not known. Each side's post leaves out what the other stresses: the first does not say she was a primary opponent, and the second does not address the reasons she gave.
next: Michigan votes on Tuesday 3 November. The result will show how the race ended.

sources.label: CNBC: Democratic Rep. Stevens endorses Republican Rogers over rival El-Sayed in Michigan Senate election
